Three options are provided for each of the four departmental subject areas. Each dataset has its own page here, built from its README, with a direct link to the EDI metadata page, a basic description, coverage, and suggested analyses.

Datasets are curated from the [Environmental Data Initiative (EDI) data portal](https://portal.edirepository.org/).

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple"}
**Note on access:** Most EDI datasets can be downloaded directly from the metadata page (or via the generated R/Python code). Some require a free EDI access key for scripted downloads. Check the “Accessing Data” documentation on the EDI site if you encounter authentication prompts.
:::

## How to choose a dataset

Use the dataset pages to compare options side by side. Each page tells you what the dataset is, where it comes from, what it contains, and which analyses it suits.

1. **Start with your interest.** Pick the subject area closest to what you want to learn about, then read its three options.
2. **Check the coverage.** Every page lists the time span and location. Look for a record long enough, or frequent enough, for your question (for example, 10-minute data supports diurnal cycles, while multi-decade records support trend analysis).
3. **Read the suggested analyses.** Each page lists analyses the dataset supports. Ask whether one of them could become your project question.
4. **Check how easy it is to access.** Open the EDI metadata page linked on each dataset page. If you hit an authentication prompt, see the access note above. MacroSheds also has an R package and a dashboard linked on its page.
5. **Ask for help if needed.** The EDI package ID is listed on every page so you can point to the exact dataset.

| Hydrology | [Hubbard Brook Daily Streamflow (New Hampshire, 1956–present)](hydrology/hubbard-brook-streamflow.qmd) | `knb-lter-hbr.2.15` |
| Hydrology | [Harvard Forest Prospect Hill Hydrological Stations (since 2005)](hydrology/harvard-forest-hydro.qmd) | `knb-lter-hfr.70` |

| Geophysics | [Interior Alaska Wildfire Effects on Permafrost Soil Temperatures (hourly, 2013–2018)](geophysics/ak-wildfire-permafrost.qmd) | `knb-lter-bnz.717.2` |

## About this site

The original README files remain in the [GitHub repository](https://github.com/EAES-380/2026-Final-Project-Data-Options). This site organizes the same content by subject so it is easier to browse.
